items.title: 29.5.2 IR Spectra of Important Functional Groups

source_refs.note: Topic 29.5.2 as printed (PDF 193-195): the alcohol, amine, amide and carboxylic acid spectra (redrawn), the NOTE, the pollutant Did You Know? box and the second Quick Check 29.2 (the book repeats the number).

blocks.text: The OH group of the alcohol shows a strong absorption at 3600-3200 cm⁻¹. The peak at 3000 cm⁻¹ is due to sp³ hybridized C−H bonds.

blocks.alt: IR spectrum of 2-butanol, CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3: % transmittance (0 to 100) against wavenumber/cm^-1 (4000 to 400). A very broad, deep band centred near 3350 is marked O-H; sharp C-H bands lie near 2950 and many bands below 1500.
blocks.caption: IR spectrum of 2-butanol (original drawing after the spectrum printed in 29.5.2).

blocks.text: The N−H bond in an amine gives rise to two weak absorptions at 3300 and 3400 cm⁻¹.

blocks.alt: IR spectrum of octylamine, CH3(CH2)7NH2: % transmittance against wavenumber/cm^-1 (4000 to 400). Two small, weak dips near 3370 and 3290 are marked N-H; very strong C-H bands near 2900 and further bands near 1600, 1470 and 800.
blocks.caption: IR spectrum of octylamine (original drawing after the spectrum printed in 29.5.2).

blocks.text: An amide exhibits absorptions above 1500 cm⁻¹ for both its N−H and C=O groups: N−H (two peaks) at 3200 and 3400 cm⁻¹; C=O at 1660 cm⁻¹.

blocks.alt: IR spectrum of propanamide, CH3CH2CONH2: % transmittance against wavenumber/cm^-1 (4000 to 400). Two strong dips near 3350 and 3180 are marked N-H, and a very strong band near 1650 is marked C=O; further sharp bands lie between 1450 and 1100.
blocks.caption: IR spectrum of propanamide (original drawing after the spectrum printed in 29.5.2).

blocks.text: The C=O group in the carboxylic acids shows a strong absorption at 1700 cm⁻¹ along with broad and deep absorption of the O-H bond of a carboxylic acid between 2500 and 3300 cm⁻¹. The broad peak caused by the O-H bond of a carboxylic acid between 2500 and 3300 cm⁻¹. This right hand side of this peak is often distorted by the peaks from C-H bonds.

blocks.alt: IR spectrum of a carboxylic acid: absorbance / % (0 at the top, 100 at the bottom) against wavenumber/cm^-1 (4000 to 500). A very broad, deep band runs from about 3700 to 2500, deepest near 3100, with small C-H bumps on its right side; a very strong band near 1750 and several strong bands between 1450 and 600.
blocks.caption: IR spectrum of a carboxylic acid (original drawing after the spectrum printed in 29.5.2).

blocks.title: NOTE
blocks.text: N-H signal in amines is broad but it is not broader than O-H signal in alcohols.

blocks.title: Did You Know?
blocks.text: Infrared spectroscopy is used to identify pollutants in vehicle emissions. The air sensors detect and measure the amount of pollutants such as carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and unburnt hydrocarbons. This commonly occurs on motorways and in busy town centres to monitor localised pollution.

items: Which one of the infra-red spectra is that of butanone and which one is of butan-2-ol?
Compounds T and U are isomers with the molecular formula C₃H₆O₂. Suggest their structures based on the spectra shown below:

blocks.alt: Two infrared spectra, A (top) and B (bottom), each plotted as absorbance / % (0 at the top, 100 at the bottom) against wavenumber/cm^-1 from 4000 to 500. A has a small dip near 3450, a strong band near 3000 and a very strong, sharp band near 1750, then several bands below 1500. B has a very broad, deep band centred near 3350, strong bands near 2950 and many bands below 1500.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 29.2 (IR): infrared spectra A and B (the book prints the spectra of Example 29.1 again here; original drawing).

blocks.alt: Two IR spectra, titled IR Spectra for Compound T (top) and IR Spectra for Compound U (bottom), each transmittance % (0 to 100) against wavenumber/cm^-1 (4000 to about 400). T has a very broad dip from about 3500 to 2500, deepest near 3000, a very strong band near 1780 and many bands below 1600. U has a flat baseline near 80 %, small bands near 2950, a very strong band near 1740 and strong bands near 1450, 1370, 1240 and 1050.
blocks.caption: Quick Check 29.2 (IR): IR spectra for compounds T and U (original drawing after the spectra printed in the Quick Check).
